### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **224** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **161** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **161**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **57** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c13c292c112e0f12ffeb0540329165e6db6c0613` — the merge of head `fee5571477bdbf70e38ed3724b5a00a6e481b12c` into base `3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c13c292c112e0f12ffeb0540329165e6db6c0613 && git checkout c13c292c112e0f12ffeb0540329165e6db6c0613
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db fee5571477bdbf70e38ed3724b5a00a6e481b12c && git checkout -B drift-repro 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db && git merge --no-ff fee5571477bdbf70e38ed3724b5a00a6e481b12c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fee5571477bdbf70e38ed3724b5a00a6e481b12c`
Local-runs: none
Reviewed-at: 2026-11-07T03:50Z
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-object-schema-mask.test.ts, content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx, .changeset/mcp-list-actions-field-mask.md + packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`summarizeAction`, `summarizeActionParams`, `collectActionDeclarations`, `systemObjectActionExposureError`, `actionPermissionError`), packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts (`resolveObjectMasker`, `maskObjectSchema`), packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.ts (`applyObjectSchemaMask`, `resolveObjectSchemaMaskPosture`, `relateObjectSchemaMaskPosture`), packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts (`maskDeniedFieldReferences`, `actionParamReadsDenied`, `presentationEntry`), packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts (`list_actions`, the `sys_*` `run_action` pre-screen, `isListableAction`, `systemObjectActionRefusal`), packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/objectstack-skill.ts, content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/ai.json, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/*.object.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts, examples/app-todo/test/mcp-actions.e2e.ts, docs/adr/0106-metadata-plane-fls-object-schema-masking.md

Read against `origin/main` at `cb8f5200002cd4e8bb6ffd6f9d3b642f2dcb8309` (merge base `5210acfbaee4a935c8bf0d79111c260797561fc0`). Every gate-carrying check on the head is `success`; the dogfood shards are queue-leg jobs and did not run on this head, which the body also reports as NOT MEASURED. The face is the changeset's own: the recogniser maps the four paths to no schema or governed face and defers to the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line, so the narrowing face it is.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff makes exactly one accept-set change and inherits one consequence of it.

**1. `list_actions` over HTTP lists an action only when the `/meta` object door would serve it to this caller, and summarises it against the object as that door serves it.** Right. ADR-0106 D1 states the rule for every plane; D5 names "any other schema-bearing endpoint" as in scope; PR #31042 brought `describe_object` and `list_objects` under the same projection; the param summary (`summarizeActionParams`) reads field label, help text, type and select options off the object, so it was the one MCP read still answering from the unprojected object. The PR does not write a second rule: `servedActionObject` hands the action to `servedToCaller` as its object's only `actions` entry, and the drop decision is `maskDeniedFieldReferences`' own (`presentationEntry` over `actions`, `actionParamReadsDenied` for `params`, `objectOverride` judged on the object it names through `relate`). The listing and the `/meta` item therefore cannot disagree about which actions exist for a caller; the new test pins the two doors equal on the fixture and pins the unrestricted and no-security controls byte-identical to before.

Two things the body under-describes, both inherited from the `/meta` rule and both correct there: (i) the drop is not only "a param binds a field the caller cannot read" — any non-prose position of the action that names such a field drops it (`visible`, `patch` keys, `defaultValue`, option predicates), by the same table the `/meta` door applies; (ii) `label`, `description`, `helpText` and the other prose keys are skipped, so an author's sentence naming a field does not cost the action. Both follow the published rule; ③ carries the documentation consequence of (i).

**2. The refusal.** A caller whose field visibility on a listed action's object cannot be evaluated, or whose projection leaves that object with no field, is refused the whole `list_actions` answer with `FIELD_VISIBILITY_UNRESOLVED` / 503. Right as written — it is D6 tier 3 and the "never an empty-fields 200" rule, and `list_objects` on `main` already refuses the whole listing on one such object, as the `/meta` list door does. Only an object with at least one otherwise-listable action reaches the projection, so an object the caller has no action on cannot trigger it. The design cost (one object's fault refuses actions on every other object) is the sibling doors' cost too and belongs to a separate rule-level step, not to this PR.

**3. The `sys_*` `run_action` side effect.** The MCP tool layer's pre-screen for a call naming a `sys_*` object admits only an action the bridge's own listing carries, so an action the projection withholds is now refused there, with the system-object sentence, and `capabilityRefusal` (which reads the declarations whole) answers nothing for it. Judged: the direction is right — the `sys_*` door already made "listed for you" the condition of running, nothing runs, and the answer for a withheld action is the same as for an action that was never declared, which is how the `/meta` door treats it. Two consequences stay open and are placed in ③: the sentence's lead names author exposure as the reason, which is not this case's reason; and the two run doors now differ on whether field readability stops a run (`sys_*` yes through the listing, every other object no). On a stock boot this changes no legitimate caller's answer, see the hunt.

**4. Unchanged, confirmed in the cited code.** `collectActionDeclarations`, the exposure, handler and permission gates, `capabilityRefusal`, `runAction` and `resumeRun` read `readServedObjects()` whole. An object-less (global) action has no object to project and is listed as declared. The stdio bridge implements no `listActions`, so `list_actions` is HTTP-only and nothing moves there.

**Consumer hunt.** Every reader of `list_actions` or its summary shape on `main`:

- `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` — the `list_actions` tool renders the summaries as-is; `run_action`'s `sys_*` pre-screen reads the listing (item 3). The tool description still promises "actions that are BOTH declared ai-exposed and that the caller is permitted to run are returned" — now a third condition applies and the string does not say so (③).
- `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts` and its console mirror `ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/objectstack-skill.ts` — the generated SKILL.md teaches "the business actions available to you (only those the app author exposed to AI and you are permitted to run)". "Available to you" stays true; the parenthesis is now incomplete (③).
- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx` — the `list_actions` row and the "two gates" paragraph state the two-condition contract; not touched by the PR (③). `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` is updated and states the projection.
- `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, `packages/mcp/README.md`, `packages/spec/src/ai/mcp.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts` — name the tool and its scope only; no promise narrows.
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/ai.json` — negative clause "list_actions advertising an action that run_action then refuses (or vice versa) is a FAIL" is now literally reachable on a non-`sys_*` object for a field-restricted persona (an action withheld from the listing that `run_action` still admits). The clause's own scope is the `ai.exposed` declaration, but the wording needs a revision note (③).
- `examples/app-todo/test/mcp-actions.e2e.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/mcp-list-actions-handler-probe.test.ts`, `mcp-list-actions-flow-params.test.ts`, `mcp-system-object-action-exposure.test.ts`, `platform-admin-action-gate.test.ts`, `domains/api-action-forward.test.ts`, `domains/mcp-package-object-discovery.test.ts` — none registers a `security` service, so the masker is the no-service passthrough and every answer is byte-identical. The dogfood `mcp-system-object-action-exposure` and `mcp-oauth-api-action-forward` suites run admin principals (D4-exempt) or an API key whose listed entries carry `unavailable`; unaffected.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/objectViewToolbarAffordances.ts`, `packages/client/src/index.ts` (`automation.listActions`, approvals `listActions`), `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/**` — different `listActions` (toolbar, automation descriptors, approval rows); not readers of this tool.
- The Console AI panel and the CLI carry no `list_actions` caller on `main`.

**Stock-boot judgment.** The only shipped `readable: false` entries are the `sys_user` `Admin` field group withheld by `member_default` / `viewer_readonly` / `external_default` (role, ban_reason, ban_expires, failed_login_count, locked_until, password_changed_at, phone_number, phone_number_verified, must_change_password, mfa_required_at, last_login_at, last_login_ip, ai_access) and the showcase `client_liaison` set's three `showcase_project` budget fields. Of the AI-exposed platform actions, the only one that names a withheld field in a non-prose position is `unlock_user` (its `visible` predicate names `locked_until`), and it is already held back from those callers by `requiredPermissions`; platform admins are D4-exempt and the admin sets keep the group readable. `invite_user` on `sys_user` names `role` only under `objectOverride: 'sys_member'`, judged on `sys_member`, where no shipped set withholds it. The self-service actions a member needs (`update_my_profile`, `resend_verification_email`) read `name`, `image`, `email_verified`, none withheld. The showcase's one exposed action is object-less. So no legitimate caller on a stock boot loses an action or receives a changed `list_actions` answer; the change bites only a deployment that authored its own field withholding, which is the population ADR-0106 addresses.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime` `patch` with a BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 `not-required` marker is the form the checklist prescribes for a non-protocol narrowing. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and the `!` in the title are consistent by construction: the `(narrowing)` arm is BREAKING, and `no` says no stated clause of the published spec moves — which holds: no schema key, export, answer member, error code or status is added or removed, and `FIELD_VISIBILITY_UNRESOLVED` is already in the ledger from PR #31042 (merged 2026-11-06T21:20:16Z). `no` is right for what the caller can no longer see as well: ADR-0106 D1 already promised a field-restricted caller exactly this answer on every plane, and the MCP security model already promised that field-level security applies to the agent as to a person, so the narrowing makes a stated promise real rather than taking a stated capability away. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right — nothing an author can write changes. `Skills-docs: no move` is right for `skills/**`; the published-docs half is answered by `connect-mcp.mdx`, with the gaps named in ③.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **(a) Other doors outside this seam still serve action param details without the caller projection** — *separate step*, as the dev reports it. D5(4) names the outlet audit; each door is its own card and its own test harness. Not this PR's scope, but the next card should be filed, not noted.
- **(b) The run doors validate params against the unprojected object** — *separate step*, and the step that also decides item ①.3's asymmetry: whether a field the caller cannot read may stop a run, and with which refusal, is a rule for the run doors (an ADR-0106 amendment or a ruling), not a listing seam's by-product. Until it is decided the two run doors answer differently by object prefix; the record names that so the next card inherits it.
- **(c) An `objectOverride` param is summarised with the label of the action's own object's same-named field** — *should-fix, separate card*. Pre-existing in `summarizeActionParams`, which ignores `objectOverride`; this PR neither widens nor narrows it, and the projection keeps the own-object label away from a caller who cannot read that field. The summary is still wrong for every caller who can.
- **`sys_*` refusal sentence** — *should-fix*. For a projection-withheld action the system-object sentence's lead ("is not exposed via MCP") names author exposure as the cause; the prescription half ("list_actions lists it for you") is the right one. A sentence whose cause is "not served to you", with the same prescription, keeps the two cases indistinguishable to the caller and stops the text pointing authors at a flag they already set.
- **Documentation states a narrower rule than the code applies** — *should-fix*. `connect-mcp.mdx` says an action is withheld when "one of its params binds a field the caller cannot read"; the rule the `/meta` door applies, and the changeset itself states, is any non-prose position of the action. The troubleshooting row should say so, and `actions-as-tools.mdx` (the `list_actions` row and the "two gates" paragraph), the `list_actions` tool description string and the generated SKILL.md text should state the third condition. The QA clause in `ai.json` needs a revision note.
- **One security question per action** — *should-fix, minor*. The projection is asked per listed action; the `/meta` list door asks once per object. Memoising the served object per object name inside one `listActions` call keeps the rule and removes the repeated asks on a boot with dozens of exposed `sys_*` actions.

### ④ Design judgment

Reusing the `/meta` projection is the right seam: it is the one place that already holds the whole rule (own-object fields, every reference position, `objectOverride` judged on the named object, D4 exemption, D6 tiers, D7 fallback set), and projecting the action as its object's sole `actions` entry gives one verdict for both doors with no table of positions copied into the bridge. The alternative — a bridge-side predicate over `params[].field` — would have been exactly the narrower rule the docs now describe, and would drift from the `/meta` door on the first new position.

Break attempts, each against the published spec on `main`:

- **`objectOverride`.** A param whose field the caller cannot read on the named object drops the action (judged there, fail-closed when that object's set cannot be determined); a param whose field they can read there is listed and its summary carries no label of this object's same-named denied field. Both pinned. The caller learns nothing of either object they are not served. Holds; the pre-existing mislabel is ③(c).
- **Global actions.** No object, nothing to project, listed as declared with inline params only. Holds. A standalone action whose `objectName` names an object the served listing omits has no `obj` either and is answered as declared; its summary then carries param names but no field detail, as on `main`. Edge, unchanged, separate.
- **Flow-backed params.** `summarizeFlowInputParams` reads the flow's variables and screen fields, never the object, and runs only when the action declares no params; the projection does not reach it and does not need to — flow metadata is not an object schema and is outside ADR-0106. Holds.
- **Actions with no params.** Listed to the restricted caller exactly as to the control, pinned; one with a `patch` naming a denied field is dropped by the field-keyed reading, which is the `/meta` answer too. Holds.
- **A caller with no readable field on the action's object.** Refused with the door's code, as `list_objects` refuses them, pinned. Holds against the published D6; the whole-listing refusal is the sibling doors' rule and is noted under ①.2 as a separate design step.
- **D4-exempt and no-service callers.** Passthrough returns the object by reference; `served.actions.length === 1` holds and the answer is byte-identical, pinned for the control and the no-security deployment.

The narrowing takes no declared capability away at the consumer — no reader of the summary shape depends on a field the caller cannot read — and makes the spec's own promise real on the one MCP read where it was not. The cited code was read, not reviewed; nothing in it must change for this PR to hold.
